provenance.note: Each promise and each status change cites a dated document; quotes checked against the source text on 2026-10-15. Five GR texts were read from the orgpedia mahGRs archive copy because the official PDF did not open; those rows say so and link both.

payload.headline: What has been promised about Nagpur's water, and by when
payload.intro: Twenty-two commitments on Nagpur's water supply, new sources, sewage and the Nag, the city's lakes, and the works at Ambazari after the flood of September 2023, each on a dated document: a Government Resolution, a court order, an NMC budget or report, the AMRUT 2.0 portal or a funder's document. Four are delivered and one is on track. One has a date moved by NMC that has not yet come; three are past their date with no delivery on record, one of them after NMC moved it. One, Lendi lake, is recorded by NMC as not completed because of opposition to removing encroachments. Twelve can be cited as promises, but their current status cannot yet be cited either way.

status_legend.delivered: The promised thing verifiably happened, even if late. The dates show how late.
status_legend.on-track: The stated date has not passed and the latest dated evidence is consistent with it.
status_legend.slipped: The institution itself has moved the date. Old and new dates are both shown.
status_legend.overdue: The promised date has passed with no delivery and no formally revised date we can cite.
status_legend.stalled: Work or approvals have stopped, by the institution's own account or a court's.
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

payload.update_model: Statuses change only against a dated citation. The register is re-checked each spring against NMC's new budget and Environment Status Report, against new Government Resolutions and the AMRUT 2.0 portal, and after hearings in the High Court and the National Green Tribunal. A passed next-check date with no new citation is flagged, never silently updated.
payload.sources_note: NMC's 2026-27 budget is a scanned Marathi document; its figures were read from the page images. Five Government Resolutions (Naik and Lendi lakes, AMRUT 2.0 water supply, the 2023 AMRUT 1.0 pipeline sanction and the Kolar-Kanhan barrage) did not open at the State's GR portal on 15 October 2026; their text was read from the orgpedia mahGRs archive copy, which each of those rows links beside the official address. Court and tribunal orders were read on Indian Kanoon; the court, case number and date are the citation. Where two official documents give different costs or lengths for the same work, both are stated.

commitments.title: Water round the clock across the city, with service targets at 5 and 10 years
commitments.committed_by: Nagpur Municipal Corporation and Nagpur Environmental Services Ltd, with the operator Orange City Water, under the contract of 3 June 2011
commitments.what: NMC's Superintending Engineer (Water Works) set out the contract's citywide targets in 2015: within 5 years, 100% coverage, 24-hour supply, working meters on every connection, 80% of complaints settled within 24 hours and 100% water quality; within 10 years, non-revenue water down from 60-70% to 20% (under 40% by year 5), 150 litres per person a day and 95% of charges collected. The slide gives years, not dates; counted from the contract of 3 June 2011 (its date in the High Court's record), the 10-year marks fell in 2021.

commitment_source.label: NMC Superintending Engineer (Water Works), '24X7 Water Initiative and Waste Water Reuse, Case Study Nagpur', ICRIER workshop, 23 February 2015, slide 14

status_history.note: By December 2014, 434 of 564 km of pipeline had been replaced (75% physical progress) and about 75,000 of a targeted 3,21,000 connections made.
status_history.source_label: NMC deck, ICRIER workshop, slide 17

status_history.note: 'Till date only 21 command areas receive 24x7 water and the rest 47 command areas are not yet covered.'
status_history.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2019-20, printed p.31 (archived copy)

status_history.note: In 2023-24, 41.91% of the 706 MLD supplied was lost between source and consumer (410 MLD billed), and parts of 36 of the 73 command areas were 'considered as dark zones since the water supply was found to be less than 2 h per day'.
status_history.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, printed pp.133-134

status_history.note: The contract is in arbitration over a rate rebasement the operator sought in February 2025. The High Court rejected NMC's application to replace the sole arbitrator appointed on 30 September 2025.
status_history.source_label: Bombay High Court (Nagpur Bench), MCA (ARBN) 278/2026, 2026:BHC-NAG:7281

commitments.title: Bring 10 TMC from the Kanhan at Lohghogari into Totladoh by tunnel
commitments.committed_by: Government of Maharashtra, Water Resources Department
commitments.what: In-principle approval to divert 10 TMC from the Kanhan near Lohghogari, in Chhindwara district of Madhya Pradesh, through a 62 km tunnel into Totladoh, to make up for the inflow the Pench has lost to Madhya Pradesh's Chaurai dam. Estimated at Rs 3,612 crore in two phases; phase 1 (Rs 17.55 crore) covers only the approvals, including Madhya Pradesh's consent, and phase 2 cannot start before them. A GR of the previous day asked the Finance Department to provide the funds within three years. The Water Resources Department's re-planning of Pench water (19 March 2020) raises NMC's share to 341 Mcum a year once the tunnel is built. No later Government document on the project was found.

commitment_source.label: Government of Maharashtra, Water Resources Department, GR PRASHAMA-2019/PK357/MOPR-2, 18 September 2019

commitments.title: Keep Futala lake clean and lay a sewer for the settlement on its bank
commitments.committed_by: NMC, on directions of the Bombay High Court (2023), the Supreme Court (2025) and the National Green Tribunal (2025-26)
commitments.what: The High Court directed on 30 November 2023 that no permanent construction be undertaken within Futala lake and that NMC and Maha Metro keep the water body clean; the Supreme Court upheld this on 7 October 2025. In the Tribunal's own case on the lake, a joint committee of CPCB, MPCB and NMC reported that about 145-160 houses beside the lake have no sewer and that the settlement has 8 cow shelters (gaushalas); on 18 November 2025 the Tribunal asked NMC for an action plan with a timeline within one month.

status_history.note: NMC reported 19 CCTV cameras and nuisance-squad rounds at the lake, and a sewer for the settlement estimated at Rs 23,63,583.

commitments.committed_by: Government of Maharashtra, through a High Level Committee under the Divisional Commissioner, Nagpur; NMC as the dam's owner
commitments.what: After the overflow of 23 September 2023, the State set up a High Level Committee to complete urgently the works taken up to strengthen Ambazari dam, citing the High Court's orders in PIL 96/2017 (21 March 2018) and PIL 56/2023. No completion date was set.

commitment_source.label: Government of Maharashtra, Urban Development Department, GR NAMPA-3023/PK261/NAVI-26, 5 January 2024

status_history.note: Rs 11 crore (Rs 1,100 lakh) budgeted for Ambazari dam strengthening in 2025-26.

status_history.note: The High Court recorded, from the affidavit placed before it, that the safety of Ambazari dam is NMC's responsibility, the dam being NMC's property.
status_history.source_label: Bombay High Court (Nagpur Bench), PIL 56/2023, order of 2 July 2025

commitments.title: Gates on Ambazari's spillway, and flood-safety measures before the monsoon
commitments.committed_by: Water Resources Department (Nagpur Irrigation Division South), by affidavit; the State's High Level Committee
commitments.what: The Irrigation Department told the High Court that the general layout and design of three escape gates, each 4 m by 2.5 m, for the spillway, which has no gates, were in progress (affidavit of 26 February 2024), and that a high-level submersible bridge across the spill had been technically sanctioned on 7 February 2024. On 8 May 2024 the court asked the High Level Committee to take essential safety measures to be completed before that monsoon. No completion date for the gates appears in the orders.

commitment_source.label: Bombay High Court (Nagpur Bench), PIL 56/2023, order of 11 July 2024 (records the affidavit of 26 February 2024)

status_history.note: Temporary flood-safety measures to be completed before the 2024 monsoon and placed on record.
status_history.source_label: Bombay High Court (Nagpur Bench), PIL 56/2023, order of 8 May 2024

status_history.note: Gate design in progress, to be sent to the Maharashtra Engineering Research Institute; NMC and other agencies to clear obstructions so the Nag downstream carries at least 75 cumecs.

commitments.title: Rebuild river and nala walls and roads damaged by the rain of September 2023
commitments.committed_by: Government of Maharashtra, Revenue and Forest Department (special package); NMC executes
commitments.what: A special package of Rs 204.72 crore for the damage of 22-23 September 2023 in the city: 8.41 km of river and nala retaining walls (Rs 163.23 crore) and 61.38 km of road repairs (Rs 41.48 crore). No completion date was set. NMC's 2025-26 budget gives the package as Rs 204.81 crore, approved on 20 February 2024.
